canonicalClauses.text: Themes are complete visual systems, not colour-only palettes. They MAY define typography, colours, surfaces, spacing defaults, control shapes, corner treatment, elevation/shadow, interaction states, animation defaults and other presentation properties, but they MUST NOT silently change the fundamental semantic meaning of controls.

Within a Theme definition, an element Definition without Type defines that Theme's default presentation for that element. A Definition with Type defines the Theme presentation for that element Type. Custom Themes SHOULD inherit another Theme when only deltas are needed.

Theme defaults, Type/Definition defaults, explicit properties, property regions, Styles, animations and runtime changes MUST all resolve through the same registered CUI property system. There MUST NOT be separate incompatible colour/layout/transform implementations for each syntax.
Theme changes at runtime MUST invalidate only affected presentation state and preserve canonical app/domain state.
Reduced motion, high contrast, scaling/zoom and non-colour-only state communication MUST be framework-level capabilities rather than app-specific reinventions.

The test harness MUST be able to render a CUI Page/Prefab at declared dimensions, Theme, scale, accessibility/reduced-motion settings and platform capability profile; interact through semantic input; inspect resulting state; and capture deterministic visual evidence where applicable.

The canonical pipeline is parse -> shorthand normalization -> symbol/import resolution -> Definition/Prefab/Theme expansion metadata -> typed property/variable/action validation -> accessibility/static lint -> dependency graph generation -> compiled CUI representation/source maps -> runtime binding.
(Definition) custom elements and Types plus built-in/custom inherited Themes including Professional, Glow, Playful, Bubble and Cinematic.

The Home shell MUST be dashboard/home-oriented rather than primarily a conventional settings application. Its stable primary navigation MUST provide at least Home/Dashboard, Apps, Library, Events, Discover, Mesh and Settings. Account/profile controls MAY live in persistent shell chrome. Chat remains a Spaces destination and MUST NOT become Home’s primary landing surface.

Home Settings owns ecosystem-wide settings only. The Settings surface MUST include at least Account & Subscription, Appearance/CUI, AI & Models, Permissions & Trust, Apps & Updates, Storage, Mesh & Devices, Privacy, Accessibility, Notifications and Advanced/Diagnostics. App-specific preferences remain in the owning app unless a setting intentionally governs multiple apps.

9to1-OS supports multiple isolated user accounts/profiles with standard and administrator roles, secure per-user data/settings/secrets, fast switching/sign-out and clearly scoped system-wide versus user-specific configuration.

Use the existing CUI typography, theme tokens, spacing, focus, menus, dialogs, tooltips, icons and persistent contextual AI bar. Labels MUST use the names in TF-01. Theme changes, reduced motion, contrast settings and scaling MUST apply to the actual editor, embedded content chrome and pop-ups. Product controls MUST not expose development jargon such as raw schema IDs, worker status or implementation notes as their ordinary labels. IDs and diagnostics belong in details/developer surfaces.

existingPublicAPIs.authority: Presentation APIs only; no profile identity, preference durability or settings mutation authority.

apis: preferences.json migration and canonical HavenPersonalisation/resource application
existingPublicAPIs.authority: Existing native Desktop preference owner, not a maintained browser platform port. CuiThemePreferenceReader reads only its havenUiThemeName field and states Desktop owns writes/migration.

apis: Haven.Application.IVersionedSettingsStore (distinct generic CRUD/export/import via VersionedAtomicSettingsStore and guarded store identity)
existingPublicAPIs.authority: These generic stores/root ABI do not publish an appearance/profile action schema, browser durability adapter or authorizing actor. Do not conflate the two IVersionedSettingsStore namespaces.

apis: LocalMotionPreferencesService actual existing OS-local ui-preferences.json owner
existingPublicAPIs.authority: Existing native read availability is explicit; failure must not become permission to animate. Browser Program.ReduceMotion presently reads actual matchMedia preference; this is not a stored Home preference or full theme profile.

sourceClosureFindings.detail: BrowserApplication.Initialize only calls CuiNativeHost.InitialisePrimitiveTheme(Home) and Write resources. No current owning appearance/profile snapshot, CAS mutation/watch or browser persistence configuration is supplied. Do not add localStorage/IndexedDB preference owner or CSS palette as substitute.

Loader applies local theme resources to scoped roots and containers without passing accessibility settings; CuiSceneVisualResources.Create also omits settings. Public loader offers SetAppearance but no public accessibility input. Applying high contrast/scale only to Application resources would be shadowed by local defaults in these paths. Actual behavioral reproduction remains NOT-RUN.

Global Apply writes CuiAppearance as only Dark/Bright, so do not infer it preserves exact SuperDark/SuperBright identity. Scene Create explicitly preserves appearance.ToString; owned live composition must retain the actual four-value selection and native ThemeVariant while passing profile accessibility.

OperatingSystemPrincipalSource returns a real SID/euid only on supported native OS; otherwise null. HomeLocalProfileIdentity uses actual guarded same-store/profile principal and is explicitly independent from AccountID/OrganisationID. A signed CAKE Account session or origin config does not mint this local-profile binding or appearance authority.

ownerRequests.recipient: Home Settings + native appearance/Platform owner via root coordination
ownerRequests.needed: Publish the actual maintained public appearance preference read/update/reset/watch API and versioned schema: exact existing theme/appearance/accessibility types, owner profile/device/app scope, trusted identity/store binding, migration/default/unavailable semantics, expected revision/CAS and receipt/unknown outcome behavior. Specify canonical storage/platform adapter and appearance event lifetime; no assumed account ownership or new browser prefs namespace.

ownerRequests.recipient: CUI Runtime/Themes owner and B1 via root
ownerRequests.needed: Expose acknowledged framework input for actual CuiAccessibilitySettings/localization through loader/container/DefaultTheme-scoped resources and native scene resources, preserving four appearances and actual theme. Reuse actual palette/token pipeline; scoped themes must inherit current accessibility rather than reset it. Live invalidation must preserve canonical state, dirty drafts, selection/focus and owner IDs.

Supply real browser-compatible current-profile authority if supported, and explicit settings scope mapping/lifetime for profile or account change; unavailable identity cannot default to fabricated principal. Clarify device-local motion preference and actual OS matchMedia precedence without introducing a second persisted preference owner.

boundedImplementationAdvice: Keep browser Settings appearance controls unavailable until an actual owner preference port is supplied; host-only acknowledged presentation snapshot can be consumed without creating persistence.

After owner snapshot is provided, validate actual CuiAccessibilitySettings; resolve actual CuiSurfacePaletteCatalog.For(surface,appearance,theme); apply through actual resource APIs on the native UI thread. Do not duplicate RGB/CSS palette or browser font/scale model.
Existing loader scoped defaults need acknowledged framework propagation before claiming contrast/scaling on actual embedded editors/popups. One global palette Apply call is insufficient.

Preserve actual four-value appearance identity and native ThemeVariant rather than reading binary Dark/Bright as a full profile; actual resource APIs create semantic tokens, but live control consumption still requires real CUI controls/journey tests.

Subscribe to owning current-profile/settings changes with generation and cancellation; dispose old profile subscriptions and private settings surfaces. Never use verified AccountID to fabricate Home local-profile actor.
acceptanceProceduresAuthoredNotRun: Real owning Settings mutation -> current profile revision/receipt, restart same canonical platform owner -> exact selection restored; forbidden/unavailable profile -> no mutation/default identity.

Actual native CUI root, scoped DefaultTheme, embedded Write editor and popup: theme/HighContrast/DisplayScale/ReduceMotion changes reach real resources/controls while canonical document IDs/revisions/dirty draft remain identical.
Switch actual profile/device/app scope according to owner policy: stale read/write/watch cannot overwrite new profile; original failure/recovery bytes retained.

Real high contrast text/focus ratios, native scale geometry/text/hit targets, keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior and exact four appearances measured against actual owner settings. Resource dictionary unit tests are supporting only.
